clues.title: Architecture: House on stilts
text: In Cambodia, wooden houses on stilts are very common. The walls are often made of vertical planks, and many homes have double or triple roofs.

clues.title: Pole: Poles
text: Cambodia for the most part uses two types of poles: a concrete ladder (or "waffle") pole, where the compartments are not holes but just indents, and a round concrete pole with holes along its whole length and a peculiar pattern in the top part. You can also rarely find wooden and thin metal poles.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Road line: Roadlines
text: Roads have dashed or solid yellow middle road lines.
Outer road lines are somewhat rare, but when present, they are solid white.
**NOTE:** Thailand uses similar road lines.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Stop sign: ឈប់/Stop
text: Stop signs in Cambodia always have the word "Stop" written in Khmer (ឈប់) in addition to the English word.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Central Plain
text: The low-lying central plain is home to most agricultural land. The landscape is flat, cultivated, and dotted with villages and farms.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Northeast
text: Conversely, the northeast is much more uncultivated: there is less agriculture and more natural vegetation. Some areas are slightly hilly.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Southwest Mountains
text: The southwest is the area with the most elevation in Cambodia. This region is characterized by hills and low mountains. Some inland roads feature dense forest cover, but the coastal areas in particular are fairly densely populated.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Southeast Light Soil
text: Sandy, white soil is very common in the region southeast of Phnom Penh, as well as around the city itself. The colour can range from bright white to slightly beige.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Northern Ridge
text: Near the northern border with Thailand, you can often see a mountainous ridgeline to your north. The soil in this region tends to be red, ranging from a slight reddish tinge to deep dark red.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Shitcam
text: Google used a weird, low-quality camera in Cambodia.
This camera is known as the official Ari (or “Shitcam”).
It has a wide circular car blur and often somewhat brownish colours.
Within Asia, India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka also have shitcam coverage.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Bollards
text: **Cambodia has a variety of different bollards. The most common ones are:**
A stone bollard with red-and-white stripes.
A stone bollard with a red top and a white base, usually with a reflector in the red part.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 3 Cars
text: **--- GENERATION 3 CARS:**
A car with a short, stubby antenna.
The antenna has three ridges.
A white car with stripes and no antenna.
There is a white stripe on the left, and a yellow stripe on the right.
This specific striped white car is unique to Cambodia.
Make sure not to mix it up with the Bangladeshi striped car, which looks slightly different.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Chevron: Chevrons
text: Chevrons in Cambodia are black with yellow arrows.
Chevrons are somewhat rare.
**Chevrons in all other Southeast Asian countries have the reverse colour scheme:**
Yellow with black arrows.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Temples
text: The majority of Cambodians are Buddhist.
Temples are common throughout the country.
Temple architecture is highly decorative, with ornamented roofs.
Thailand and Laos are also majority Buddhist.
Temples in these countries can look similar.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Tiled & Red Roofs
text: Many traditional homes have tiled orange or red roofs, sometimes with ornaments on the ridges and corners.
Corrugated and plain metal roofs are also common.
On other, more modern buildings, you can see a wider variety of roof colours and materials.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Blue Windows
text: **Traditional Cambodian wooden stilt houses tend to have very recognizable colour schemes:**
Walls are commonly painted dark red-brown, light blue or an ochre orange.
Doors, windows and other architectural details are often painted bright blue.
More modern houses tend to have a wider variety of colour schemes.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Road 48 Bollard
text: **Black-and-white bollards** in Cambodia are only found on Road 48, between Tatai and the intersection with Road 4.
**NOTE:** Make sure to check other clues before guessing, because this style of bollard is commonly found in Thailand.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Road 4 Bollard
text: Unique **triangular bollards** with red stripes can be found in three places in Cambodia, all located in the same area in the southwest:
On Road 4 between Angk Snuol and Preah Sihanouk. They are especially common in the section between Kirirom National Park and Preah Sihanouk.
One small off-road of Road 4, in Ream National Park near Preah Sihanouk.
In Preah Monivong National Park.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: waffel
text: Concrete ladder poles (so named because the indents and ridges resemble a ladder).

NOTE: You can easily distinguish between Thailand and Cambodia based on the poles. Thailand uses square concrete poles with rows of small pinholes on the sides. Such poles are very uncommon in Cambodia (but not completely absent).
